scope: Bounded Part4 narrated/history-card claims and six bibliography book records; source-level primary/issuer/publisher evidence, not exhaustive history or visual/audio reapproval.

claims.claim: Leibniz Nova methodus printed1684; dx/dy; Newton fluxions1660s; first printed calculus.
claims.evidence: Smithsonian original-item catalog confirms author, October1684 Acta eruditorum extract, pp467–473.
claims.limits: Original pages and priority comparison were not read; dx/dy and Newton1660s were not independently established from original manuscripts in this pass.

claims.claim: Lagrange1788 Mecanique analytique, constrained mechanics/multipliers.
claims.evidence: HKUST institutional rare-book catalog confirms first edition, author, Paris publisher and1788.
claims.limits: Original multiplier passage not inspected. This is not proof that1788 was first discovery; no invention-priority correction asserted.

claims.claim: Cauchy1847 three-page note, orbit equations, sum-of-squares descent.
claims.evidence: Original journal table-of-contents transcription identifies title at536; repository cites536–538. Original BnF page was located.
claims.limits: BnF original returned403. Orbit/sum-of-squares wording not verified from original text; secondary Lemarechal is listed in README but not substituted for primary evidence.

claims.claim: Walking downhill is the oldest method in this series.
claims.evidence: Literal superlative conflicts with this part’s earlier dated calculus and Newton root method. Parent authorized changing only the English sentence and its Chinese narration lookup/value. Replacement: Walking downhill this way is a standard optimization method.
claims.limits: Source/bilingual validation only. Fresh rendered Gradient case identities and revised timing require parent regression; old outputs retain historical identities.

claims.claim: Karush1939 Chicago masters thesis gives inequality optimality conditions.
claims.evidence: Institutional catalog target was identified but could not be read.
claims.limits: Catalog access403; no original thesis read and no credentials/paywall bypass attempted. This pass neither validates the full theorem/priority wording nor declares it false.

claims.claim: Kuhn and Tucker1951 nonlinear programming conditions.
claims.evidence: UCPress publisher chapter citation confirms authors,1951,pp481–492. Berkeley catalog search metadata dates the symposium1950.
claims.limits: Full chapter unavailable;1951 is publication year, not a verified discovery date. Berkeley page403. Constraint qualification statement was not re-proved from original chapter.

claims.claim: Wengert1964, General Electric, elementary program steps carrying values and derivatives.
claims.evidence: Publisher-deposited abstract/metadata mirrored by CiNii confirms author affiliation, CACM7(8)463–464,August1964 and elementary-step derivative method.
claims.limits: ACM page403; publisher abstract mirror, not full original paper, was read. No priority claim beyond the actual dated example validated.

claims.claim: Linnainmaa1970 masters thesis on reverse accumulation/roundoff,1976 BIT paper.
claims.evidence: 1976 publisher abstract describes Taylor coefficients for local roundoff; its reference2 explicitly cites the1970 Helsinki masters thesis and title.
claims.limits: 1970 thesis existence/title supported through the author’s published citation; Finnish original and reverse algorithm were not inspected. Not a complete first-invention audit.

claims.claim: Werbos1974 Harvard thesis proposes network training; worked out1982.
claims.evidence: Author-hosted retrospective says ordered-derivative chain rule was proved in his1974 Harvard thesis. Author-hosted1990 original paper page1 was inspected via scanned-page OCR and discusses the general backward derivative method and1974 dynamic-model application.
claims.limits: 1974 thesis itself and1982 application were not read; author retrospective supports general1974 link but not the exact network-priority/1982 sentence. OCR page1 is partial and not a thesis substitute.

claims.claim: Kelley1960 and Bryson1961 backward recursions for flight paths/control.
claims.evidence: Actual scene claim and README attribution were inventoried. No original control paper was read in this bounded pass.
claims.limits: Dates/technical priority remain unverified here; README currently points to a later history review.

claims.claim: Rumelhart,Hinton,Williams1986 learn hidden representations using backprop.
claims.evidence: Nature publisher abstract explicitly connects backward weight adjustment with hidden units learning task-relevant features; author/date/volume/pages agree.
claims.limits: Publisher abstract only; no claim that these authors invented all backpropagation.

claims.claim: IEEE7541985 standardizes binary formats, operations and rounding; Kahan a principal architect.
claims.evidence: IEEE issuer page confirms1985 publication and binary formats/basic operations/exceptions scope. Berkeley institutional Kahan bio calls him the primary architect.
claims.limits: Detailed1985 normative rounding clauses not accessed; full standard not purchased. Attribution denotes major contribution, not sole authorship. Current2019 standard was not substituted for1985 clauses.

claims.claim: Micikevicius etal2022 E4M3/E5M2 layouts; E4M3 maximum448, no infinities.
claims.evidence: Original arXiv v2 section3/Table1 gives4/3 and5/2 fields, E4M3 finite max448/no infinity and E5M2 IEEE-like special values.
claims.limits: 2022 dates these particular proposed encodings, not invention of all8-bit floating point. Paper itself cites prior FP8 work. No universal claim all training arithmetic is8bit validated.

claims.claim: Griewank1992 recursive checkpointing: log storage, log overhead, nlogn total work.
claims.evidence: Publisher abstract bounds temporal and spatial growth relative to original evaluation by a logarithmic factor;1992 issue date confirmed (online posting2011 is distinct).
claims.limits: Abstract-level asymptotic support; not a proof of this repository’s physical-memory use.

claims.claim: Chen,Xu,Zhang,Guestrin2016 sqrt-depth checkpointing for deep networks.
claims.evidence: Original abstract and introductory/related-work sections describe O(sqrt(n)) memory with recomputation and explicitly acknowledge existing AD checkpointing.
claims.limits: Supports bringing the method to deep nets, not first invention of checkpointing; model assumptions apply.

claims.claim: FlashAttention recomputes attention weights in backward pass.
claims.evidence: Actual claim inventoried but original FlashAttention paper was not inspected in this bounded pass.
claims.limits: Existing source claim is not independently certified here.

claims.claim: Newton1669,Raphson1690,Simpson1740 multivariate/minimum developments.
claims.evidence: SIAM confirms cited Ypma1995 historical article and bibliography identity.
claims.limits: Original17th/18th-century works were not read; publisher historical-article identity is not primary verification of every date/detail.

claims.claim: Pearlmutter1994 fast exact Hv without forming H, cost comparable to gradient.
claims.evidence: MITPress original publisher abstract describes direct Hessian-vector multiplication through the R operator, avoiding explicit Hessian with gradient-comparable computational cost.
claims.limits: Exact refers to derivative algorithm versus finite differences; no claim of zero floating-point error.

claims.claim: Boser,Guyon,Vapnik1992 optimal-margin classifier dual/support patterns.
claims.evidence: Conference record preserves original abstract: margin maximization and solution using supporting patterns; authors,COLT1992,pp144–152,DOI agree.
claims.limits: Linked legacy svms.org PDF redirected to unrelated content; not accepted as paper evidence. Original dual derivation/intercept equality not read in this pass, so support limited to abstract/metadata.

claims.claim: Cortes and Vapnik1995 Support-vector networks.
claims.evidence: Springer publisher confirms title, authors,September1995,MachineLearning20 pp273–297.
claims.limits: No full-paper theorem/algorithm audit.

claims.claim: Bai,Kolter,Koltun2019 fixed-point/equilibrium networks and implicit gradients.
claims.evidence: Original preprint abstract describes rootfinding for weight-tied fixed points and implicit differentiation;2019 initial submission and NeurIPS reference agree.
claims.limits: Supports paper example, not global convergence of every learned fixed point or this repository’s toy implementation.

claims.claim: Amos and Kolter2017 differentiable optimization/QP layers.
claims.evidence: Original preprint abstract describes optimization layers and differentiating through them;initial2017 submission/ICML2017 agree.
claims.limits: Abstract-level example check, not every solver assumption.

claims.claim: Rajeswaran etal2019 iMAML implicit differentiation through inner optimization.
claims.evidence: Original abstract describes gradients based on the inner optimum rather than differentiating the entire optimization path;2019 authors/date agree.
claims.limits: Abstract-level example check; approximation and inner-stationarity conditions remain relevant.

claims.claim: Six listed book author/edition/year entries.
claims.evidence: Publisher/author metadata agrees: GriewankWalther2ed2008;NocedalWright2ed2006;BoydVandenberghe2004;Higham2ed2002;GoodfellowBengioCourville2016. BlondelRoulet2024 author citation explicitly labels arXiv book draft/preprint.
claims.limits: Metadata check only, not reading or approving all textbook content.2024 Elements is a book draft/preprint, not a verified2024commercial-edition claim.

limits: No production render, numerical compute, cache mutation, full paper redistribution, paid access, new credentials, local-computer action, commit or push by reviewer.
Unreviewed original thesis details and priority claims remain explicitly limited. Metadata-only is not full-text support.
Remaining README paper entries/framework chronology/Jaynes dice story/saddle literature were not exhaustively checked.
Sources were read through public web snapshots during2026-11-01; no inference that a date alone validates all surrounding narration.
